subject.title: [Bug]: Cron agent jobs silently time out during sustained LLM API outages instead of fast-failing on definitive errors

question: For plain provider messages like `LLM error api_error: Internal server error`, should OpenClaw treat them as shared provider cooldown signals, cron-local transient retry signals, or only generic timeouts?
rationale: Classifying plain 500s as shared cooldown can fast-skip same-provider fallbacks but may poison provider health for ambiguous errors; keeping them as timeout may preserve safety but still needs proof that cron no longer burns the outer timeout.

options.title: Cron-local transient server error
options.body: Classify the cron-visible run error as retryable `server_error` without marking shared auth-profile cooldown unless the provider error is structured enough.

options.title: Shared provider cooldown
options.body: Treat plain API internal-server failures as provider outage signals and skip same-provider candidates across runs, accepting broader cooldown effects.

options.title: Keep timeout-only with proof
options.body: Leave plain provider 500 text as timeout only if a focused cron/fallback test proves the run fast-fails before the outer deadline.

recommendation.title: Cron-local transient server error
recommendation.body: Classify the cron-visible run error as retryable `server_error` without marking shared auth-profile cooldown unless the provider error is structured enough.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged structured `server_error` work is the closest recent provenance for this policy boundary.
